chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mansur ibn Yunus, from al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three things are deliverers and three things are destroyers.' They asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the deliverers?' He said: 'Fearing Allah in secret as though you see Him, for if you do not see Him, surely He sees you; exercising justice in happiness and anger; and moderation in abundance and poverty.' They asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, and what are the destroyers?' He said: 'Vain desire that is followed, stinginess that is obeyed, and a person being pleased with himself.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that save a person and the three things that destroy them according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* encapsulates the core of Shia asceticism by linking internal states to external conduct, emphasizing that true piety (*Taqwa*) is rooted in the awareness of God's omniscience even in solitude. The inclusion of 'moderation in wealth' (*Qasd*) alongside emotional justice highlights the holistic nature of spiritual salvation, balancing inner mindfulness with practical self-restraint. This teaching serves as a foundational ethical framework for distinguishing between the purifying effects of divine consciousness and the corrupting influence of ego-driven desires.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 15.Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from al-Thumālī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (a) who said, “The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said, ‘Three things deliver [one to safety] and three things destroy.’ They asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, what are the things that save [a person]?’ He said, ‘Fearing Allah in secret as though you see Him, for if you cannot see Him, surely He can see you; exercising justice in happiness and anger; and [thirdly,] moderation in [times of] abundance and poverty.’ They asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, and what are the destroyers?’ He (ṣ) said, ‘Vain desire that is followed, the adoption of stinginess, and for a person to be pleased with himself.’”
